key_insight: A clustering-based wrapper feature selection method (CSFS) can match classic sequential selection performance for renewable energy prediction while cutting computation time.
engineering_relevance: Better feature selection can make wind and solar power forecasting pipelines faster, more reliable, and easier to deploy in real-world energy systems.
method: Cluster features first, then run sequential wrapper selection within and across clusters.
Model-agnostic design for renewable energy prediction pipelines.
Compared against SFS, filter methods, and Random Forest feature importance.
evidence_signal: Across two real-world renewable energy use cases, the authors found wrapper-based methods performed best overall, and CSFS matched SFS while reducing computational cost by about 21%.
watch_item: Results come from specific wind turbine and photovoltaic prediction settings, so performance and selected features may not transfer unchanged to other datasets or forecasting models.
paper_title: Improving Wind and Solar Power Prediction with Efficient Wrapper-based Feature Selection: An Empirical Study
